Psilocybin, a tryptamine-derived alkaloid from Psilocybe mushrooms, has emerged as a high-value biopharmaceutical candidate due to its promising applications in mental health. While clinical studies highlight its rapid and sustained antidepressant effects, current challenges lie in achieving scalable, reproducible, and cost-effective production to meet growing research and therapeutic demand.

In contrast, biotechnological approaches have demonstrated significant progress toward sustainable production. Heterologous expression of psilocybin biosynthetic genes in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Aspergillus nidulans has enabled improved metabolic flux and precursor availability, reaching titers over 200 mg/L under optimized conditions.
